invariants.requirement: Treat created, updated, and unchanged as successful episode outcomes; count is transaction write volume, not a presence or success gate.
After a successful outcome, verify nodes through the type-aware query path a reader will use before marking the source ingested.

Treat timeout, empty response, gateway errors, and HTTP 408 as indeterminate commit results. Make two control-gated reads separated by 15 seconds; only two absences permit one byte-identical retry. Two absences still do not prove non-commit.

Search before minting and compare the actual destination IRI, not only its label. Reuse an existing addressable canonical name exactly; report other IRIs sharing its label. A retry must preserve the exact episode body.

Omit description on reused episode nodes while retaining their governed type. Current servers revise attributed descriptions and can refuse ambiguous legacy comments. Use /set for a deliberate predicate correction, then verify its value and count.

Use /knot or /set with exact RDF predicate IRIs for explicit predicate writes. Current /episode also preserves supported standard prefixes and angle-bracket full IRIs; never sanitize a standard predicate into a local lookalike.

Every episode node, including reuse, has a governed type; one untyped node invalidates the whole episode. Each name occurs once per episode; add another type in a separate episode without a description.
